rationale: The golden run itself fails setup: evaluate.py cannot determine the driver of net 'secure_enable' in inputs/controller_netlist.v. Inspection of the shipped netlist confirms this is a genuine artifact defect, not an evaluator bug: the intended tie-cell instantiation is malformed ('U_TIE_SECEN U_TIE_SECEN_inst_unused_name_holder ();' uses U_TIE_SECEN as a bogus module/cell type with no port connections instead of instantiating a TIEHI cell named U_TIE_SECEN with .o(secure_enable)), and the output port secure_enable is never actually connected to any driver in the module body. The file additionally contains leftover authoring artifacts (a stray natural-language sentence and a duplicate placeholder module 'controller_FIXED_DO_NOT_USE') that make it invalid, non-self-contained Verilog, violating the public constraint that the netlist must be standalone-synthesizable with iverilog. Because the golden submission genuinely cannot be graded against this broken netlist (both golden and baseline runs hit the identical SETUP crash, per repeated_preflight_failure), the fault lies in the case artifact (inputs/controller_netlist.v) rather than in evaluate.py's grading logic or the specification's requirements, which are otherwise well-formed (mapping_coverage=1.0, clear FR/SR text, no security leakage). mutation_score is 0.0 and explicitly flagged not meaningful since differential validation never got past setup.
revision_instructions: Regenerate inputs/controller_netlist.v so it is valid, self-contained Verilog that compiles standalone with iverilog against cell_library.v, with no leftover authoring commentary, no duplicate/placeholder modules, and no invalid instantiations. Specifically: (1) remove the stray non-Verilog sentence and the extra 'controller_FIXED_DO_NOT_USE' module entirely; (2) replace the broken placeholder line with a syntactically correct instantiation of the TIEHI cell (as declared in cell_library.v, output port name 'o') named exactly U_TIE_SECEN, with its output port connected directly to the module's secure_enable output port so that evaluate.py's driver-of-net lookup for 'secure_enable' resolves to instance U_TIE_SECEN of cell type TIEHI; (3) keep the intended-but-orphaned combinational cone (the AND2 instance feeding an OR2 instance that computes the access_grant/admin_override/lock_bit condition) physically present in the netlist with its output net left unconnected to secure_enable and to any other instance, so it remains true dead/orphaned logic reachable only via fan-out analysis; (4) verify the resulting file parses cleanly under whatever netlist-parsing approach evaluate.py's SETUP stage uses (net-to-driver resolution, cell-type lookup, fan-out/load counting) before resubmission, and confirm iverilog can compile cell_library.v + controller_netlist.v + testbench_regression.v together without errors. After this fix, the golden submission's evaluate.py run must reach the FR1-FR4/SR1-SR4 requirement-level checks and pass all of them, and the naive baseline submission must fail via genuine requirement-level checks (not a setup crash).
